# New renderings, iliad-119 (18.310–409)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἐλαφηβόλος (ἀνήρ, 18.319) | "deer-shooting" | "deer-shooting" | "deer-hunting", "stag-slaying"; ἔλαφος "deer" + βάλλω "strike, shoot" |
| λὶς ἠϋγένειος (18.318) | "fine-bearded lion" | "fine-bearded lion" | follows the table’s ἠϋγένειος (15.275) |
| ὕλης ἐκ πυκινῆς (18.320) | "out of close-packed forest" | "out of the close-packed forest" | "thick wood", "dense woodland" (11.155 ἀξύλῳ ὕλῃ), "solid"; πυκινός literal sense "close-packed", ὕλη "forest" (5.52) |
| ἁδινοῦ γόοιο (18.316) | "the thronging lament" | "the thronging lament" | "heavy", "vehement", "ceaseless"; follows the table’s ἁδινός "thronging" (2.87, 2.469) and ἐξῆρχε γόοιο "led off the lament" (18.51) |
| ἀποδειροτομήσω (18.336) | "I shall cut the throats of" | "I shall cut the throats of" (+ note: throat-cutting or beheading not settled) | "behead", "slaughter", "sacrifice"; ἀπο- + δειρή "neck" + τέμνω |
| ἐρεῦσαι (ὁμοίην γαῖαν, 18.329) | "to redden" | "to redden" | "to stain", "to soak"; ἐρεύθω as in the table’s αἵματι γαῖαν ἐρεύθων (11.394); blood understood, not added |
| κτεριῶ (18.334) | "I shall render … funeral rites" | "I shall pay … funeral honours" | "bury"; follows the table’s κτεριοῦσι (11.455) |
| καμόμεσθα (18.341) | "toiled for" | "toiled" | "won", "captured" (the Greek has only κάμνω "toil"); second-aorist middle |
| πιείρας (πόλεις, 18.342) | "rich" | "rich" | "fat", "fertile", "prosperous"; πίειρα "rich, fat" |
| ἑανῷ λιτί (18.352) | "a fine linen" | "fine linen" | "soft cloth", "linen robe"; ἑανός "fine, soft" (table: a fine robe), λιτί a rare word for linen cloth |
| λεχέεσσι (18.352) | "a bed" | "a bed" | "bier" (kept for φέρτρον, 18.236), "couch"; follows the table’s λεχέεσσι "bed" (18.233); the note says it is the bier |
| κηλέῳ (πυρί, 18.346) | "blazing" | "blazing" | "burning", "bright", "kindled"; κήλεος, dictionary gloss, used of fire only |
| ἀλείφατος ἐννεώροιο (18.351) | "ointment nine years old" | "ointment nine years old" | "oil" (kept for ἔλαιον in the same sentence), "salve"; ἐννέωροι "nine years old" (11.311) |
| ἐν … πλῆσαν (ὠτειλάς, 18.351) | "filled in" | "filled" | "stuffed", "packed"; tmesis, genitive of the filling |
| ἤνοπι χαλκῷ (18.349) | "gleaming bronze" | "gleaming bronze" | "bright", "shining" (reserved for φαεινός); **departs from the Odyssey**: the line is the Odyssey’s (10.360, odyssey-048, "bright bronze"), but the Iliad table’s own row (16.408, iliad-103) is "gleaming bronze" and rejects "bright"; the Iliad row governs here, and the validator may warn on the difference |
| Χάρις λιπαροκρήδεμνος (18.382) | "Charis of the sleek head-veil" | "Charis of the sleek head-veil" | "bright-veiled", "of the shining veil", "with glossy hair-band"; λιπαρός "sleek" (table: 2.44, 9.156), κρήδεμνον "head-veil" (5.346); picture not certain; name kept as "Charis", not "Grace" |
| ὤπυιε (18.383) | "had married" | "had married" | "had as wife", "took to wife"; follows the table’s ὄπυιε "married" (16.178) |
| κυλλοποδίων (Ἥφαιστος, 18.371) | "the crook-footed one" | "the crook-footed god" | "lame" (kept for χωλός, 18.397), "club-footed", "bandy-legged"; κυλλός "crooked" + πούς |
| ἄφθιτον … δόμον (18.370) | "unfailing" | "unfailing" | "imperishable", "undying" (the table keeps those off ἄφθιτος, 2.46) |
| ἐϋσταθέος μεγάροιο (18.374) | "well-standing" | "sturdy" | "well-founded", "well-built"; follows the table’s ἐϋσταθής (20.258) |
| σφ’ ὑπὸ κύκλα … πυθμένι (18.375) | "beneath each one at the base" | "under the base of each" | "bottom", "foot"; πυθμήν "base" (11.635) |
| οὔατα (of the tripods, 18.378) | "ears" | "ears" | "handles"; the note says they are handles shaped like ears |
| δεσμούς (κόπτε, 18.379) | "bonds" | "bonds" | "rivets", "fastenings"; the note says probably rivets |
| ἤρτυε (18.379) | "was fitting" | "was fitting" | "was preparing", "was setting in order" (kept for ἀρτύνω, 15.303) |
| κάλυκας (18.401) | "flower-cups" | "flower-cups" | "rosettes", "buds", "earrings"; exact form not known (note says so) |
| ἕλικας (18.401) | "spirals" | "spirals" | "twisting rings", "bracelets", "curls"; the table’s ἕλικας βόας "crumple-horned" is a different sense (curled) |
| πόρπας (18.401) | "brooches" | "brooches" | "clasps", "pins" |
| ἀψορρόου Ὠκεανοῖο (18.399) | "back-flowing Oceanus" | "back-flowing Oceanus" | follows the table’s ἀψόρροος Ὠκεανός (20.65) |
| κόλπῳ (Εὐρυνόμη τε Θέτις θ’ ὑπεδέξατο κόλπῳ, 18.398) | "in her bosom" | "in her bosom" | "in their bosom", "in the folds"; singular verb and noun follow the nearer subject; follows the table’s 6.136 row |
| κυνώπιδος (of Hera, 18.396) | "dog-faced" | "shameless" | "dog-eyed", "bitch"; applies the Odyssey-pair row (3.180); not the Iliad’s vocative "you dog-face" (1.159) |
| ζῳάγρια (18.407) | "the life-price" | "the price of my life" | "reward for saving my life"; follows the table’s ζωάγρια (8.462) |
| ὅπλα (smith’s gear, 18.409) | "gear" | "gear" | "tools" (the thought), "arms", "weapons"; keeps the table’s ὅπλα "the gear" (12.410); the sense here is the smith’s equipment |
| ξεινήϊα (18.408) | "gifts of hospitality" | "the gifts due a guest" | "guest-gifts" ; the same wording as the Odyssey’s ξείνια at 18.387 (odyssey-022) |
| ἄλοχος κασιγνήτη (Ἥρη, 18.356) | "his sister and wife" | "his sister and wife" | "sister-wife", "consort" (kept for παράκοιτις) |
| Ζεὺς δ’ Ἥρην προσέειπε κασιγνήτην ἄλοχόν τε (18.356, whole-line speech introduction) | "And Zeus addressed Hera, his sister and wife:" | "And Zeus spoke to Hera, his sister and wife:" | "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο); προσέειπε "addressed" / "spoke to", as in the table’s reply rows |
| ἔπρηξας καὶ ἔπειτα (18.357) | "You accomplished it, even so" | "You have accomplished it after all" | "You have done it again", "you got your way"; πρήσσω "accomplish" (11.552), object unstated |
| ἦ ῥά νυ (18.358, 18.394) | "truly then" / "truly now" | "truly then" / "truly" | "can it be that…?" (asseverative reading preferred, with irony in the note) |
| ἔκβαλον ἅλιον ἔπος (18.324) | "a vain word I threw out" | "it was a vain word I threw out" | "an idle word", "a word spoken in vain"; ἅλιος "vain" (4.26, 4.158) |
| ἀνέστη … ἀνστήσασ’ (18.358) | "having made … rise up" | "by making … rise up" | "rousing" (kept for ἐγείρω), "raising"; transitive aorist of ἀνίστημι |
| κέκλετο δ’ Ἥφαιστον κλυτοτέχνην εἶπέ τε μῦθον (18.391, whole-line speech introduction) | "And she called on Hephaestus, famous in craft, and spoke a word:" | "She called on Hephaestus, famous in craft, and spoke to him:" | "called to", "gave orders to" (the table’s rendering where the speaker commands; Charis does not command); "called on" as the table’s κέκλετ’ Ὀδυσσεύς (11.312) |
| ὣς ἄρα φωνήσασα πρόσω ἄγε δῖα θεάων (18.388, whole line) | "So then, having spoken, she led her forward, heavenly-one of goddesses." | "With these words she led her forward, heavenly even among goddesses." | "she spoke and led"; follows the table’s ὣς ἄρα φωνήσασα λίπε σπέος (18.65) and δῖα θεάων; the epithet belongs to Charis, not Thetis |
| ἔν τ’ ἄρα οἱ φῦ χειρὶ … (female subject, female object, 18.384) | "And she clasped her by the hand, and spoke a word, and called her by name:" | "she took her hand, and spoke, calling her by name:" | "him" (the published 6.253 rendering, male object); table’s 6.253 and 6.485 rows give the pronoun by sex; merged with 382–383 into one unit so that the validator’s identical-unit rule does not force "him" |
